claims.text: Role in hyperkalemia: ECG changes (loss of P wave or wide QRS): IV calcium + insulin and glucose; 10 to 20 mL of 10% calcium gluconate IV over 5 to 10 minutes;
claims.quote: If ECG changes include the loss of P-wave or widening of the QRS complex, treatment with IV calcium as well as insulin and glucose is indicated; 10 to 20 mL of 10% calcium gluconate (or 5 to 10 mL of 22% calcium gluceptate) is given IV over 5 to 10 minutes.

claims.text: works within minutes but lasts only 20 to 30 minutes: a temporizing measure until other tx work or dialysis starts;
claims.quote: The benefits of calcium occur within minutes but last only 20 to 30 minutes. Calcium infusion is a temporizing measure while awaiting the effects of other treatments or initiation of hemodialysis and may need to be repeated.
Calcium should be given with caution to patients taking digoxin because of the risk of precipitating hypokalemia-related arrhythmias.

claims.text: Avoid in pts receiving cardiac glycosides; if necessary, give slowly in small amounts w/ close ECG monitoring.
claims.quote: Administration of Calcium Gluconate in Sodium Chloride Injection should be avoided in patients receiving cardiac glycosides. If concomitant therapy is necessary, Calcium Gluconate in Sodium Chloride Injection should be given slowly in small amounts and with close ECG monitoring
claims.locator: 5.1 Arrhythmias with Concomitant Cardiac Glycoside Use

claims.quote: Do not administer Ceftriaxone simultaneously with Calcium Gluconate in Sodium Chloride Injection via a Y-site in any age group.

claims.text: Calcinosis cutis can occur w/ or w/o extravasation; tissue necrosis, ulceration, and secondary infection are the most serious complications.
claims.quote: Calcinosis cutis can occur with or without extravasation of Calcium Gluconate in Sodium Chloride Injection, is characterized by abnormal dermal deposits of calcium salts, and clinically manifests as papules, plaques, or nodules that may be associated with erythema, swelling, or induration. Tissue necrosis, ulceration, and secondary infection are the most serious complications.

claims.text: If extravasation or calcinosis cutis signs occur, stop IV at that site immediately and treat as needed.
claims.quote: If extravasation occurs or clinical manifestations of calcinosis cutis are noted, immediately discontinue intravenous administration at that site and treat as needed.

claims.text: Rapid injection may cause vasodilation, ↓BP, bradycardia, arrhythmias, syncope, and cardiac arrest; infuse slowly.
claims.quote: Rapid injection of Calcium Gluconate in Sodium Chloride Injection may cause vasodilation, decreased blood pressure, bradycardia, cardiac arrhythmias, syncope and cardiac arrest. To avoid adverse reactions that may follow rapid intravenous administration, Calcium Gluconate in Sodium Chloride Injection should be infused slowly.
claims.locator: 5.4 Hypotension, Bradycardia, and Cardiac Arrhythmias with Rapid Administration

claims.text: Measure serum Ca every 4 to 6 h during intermittent infusions and every 1 to 4 h during continuous infusion.
claims.quote: Measure serum calcium every 4 to 6 hours during intermittent infusions with Calcium Gluconate in Sodium Chloride Injection and measure serum calcium every 1 to 4 hours during continuous infusion.

claims.text: OD may cause hypercalcemia; symptoms typically develop when total serum Ca is ≥12 mg/dL.
claims.quote: Overdosage of Calcium Gluconate in Sodium Chloride Injection may result in hypercalcemia. Symptoms of hypercalcemia typically develop when the total serum calcium concentration is ≥12 mg/dL.

claims.text: If OD occurs, stop administration immediately and give supportive tx to restore intravascular volume and promote urinary Ca excretion if needed.
claims.quote: If overdose of Calcium Gluconate in Sodium Chloride Injection occurs immediately discontinue administration and provide supportive treatments to restore intravascular volume as well as promote calcium excretion in the urine if necessary.
